key_insight: Biasing initialization toward stiff, flat hinges steers origami optimization toward physically favorable basins, improving discrete-design success without additional compute.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness can make gradient-based design more reliable when continuous relaxations must become discrete material or component choices.
method: Use automatic differentiation and bilevel optimization to assign four discrete hinge types on fixed origami geometries.
Bias initialization toward the stiff, flat hinge option while leaving optimization unchanged.
Alternatively, penalize frustration and floppiness directly in the outer loss.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 97% success for relaxed baseline designs but only 49% after discretization; the initialization prior raises discrete success to 69%, and physical penalties raise it to 78%.
watch_item: The demonstrated gains concern a fixed-geometry origami design problem; transfer to other geometries or discrete engineering choices remains unestablished.
paper_title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
